Definition: a prolonged form of the poetical μάκαρ (meaning the same); supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off:-- blessed, happy(X -ier).
BiblicalUsage: Makarios means blessed, happy, supremely blest, and it opens the Sermon on the Mount. Matthew 5:3 says blessed are the poor in spirit, and Matthew 5:6 says blessed are they which hunger and thirst after righteousness. Luke 6:20 says blessed be ye poor, for yours is the kingdom of God, and James 1:12 says blessed is the man that endureth temptation, for he shall receive the crown of life.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word turns the world's idea of blessing upside down: the poor, the mourning, the hungry, and the tempted are the blessed ones. My position is that James 1:12 is the promise that makes the Beatitudes livable, because the blessing is not just a feeling now but a crown of life then.
